hazard: Insufficient visibility of pedestrians by high-fronted goods vehicles

promises.quote: will endeavour to explain the current legislation on vehicle construction matters and the steps being taken to address your concerns
promises.summary: explain legislation and steps to address concerns

concerns.quote: That whilst the relevant EU Directives (2003/97/EC and 2005/27/EC) and associated legal requirements for some high-fronted goods vehicles require the fitting of a 'front blind spot mirror' (Class VI) of a certain size, shape and resulting view, the actual shape (convex) and size of such mirrors does not provide sufficient visibility of slow moving pedestrians (especially the elderly), or those not wearing highly visible clothing, especially when very close to the front of the vehicle.
concerns.hazard: insufficient visibility of pedestrians by high-fronted goods vehicles

promises.quote: the DfT is working at international level to develop appropriate requirements to improve vision for drivers around large goods vehicles. This work includes improved direct vision for the driver through vehicle windows and the windscreen, a moving-off information system to provide a warning to the driver if a vulnerable road user is in front of a vehicle, a blind spot information system to detect cyclists alongside vehicles and provide a warning to the driver, and reversing detection using cameras
promises.summary: Develop international requirements for improved driver vision and safety systems

concerns.quote: standard class 5 and 6 mirrors create an avoidable risk cab drivers will not see other road users and pedestrians in close proximity to the cab when stationary
concerns.hazard: inadequate visibility of pedestrians near stationary lorries
